bug_description.original: Detailed report: https://oss-fuzz.com/testcase?key=5629878397829120 Project: harfbuzz Fuzzer: libFuzzer_harfbuzz_hb-subset-fuzzer Fuzz target binary: hb-subset-fuzzer Job Type: libfuzzer_msan_harfbuzz Platform Id: linux Crash Type: Use-of-uninitialized-value Crash Address: Crash State: bool hb_vector_t<hb_set_t::page_map_t, 1u>::bfind<hb_set_t::page_map_t> hb_set_t::page_map_t const* hb_vector_t<hb_set_t::page_map_t, 1u>::bsearch<hb_se hb_set_t::page_for Sanitizer: memory (MSAN) Recommended Security Severity: Medium
bug_description.normalized: OSS-Fuzz issue 10097: harfbuzz MSan use-of-uninitialized-value in the hb-subset-fuzzer. While subsetting a malformed font, the GSUB closure iterates the Coverage subtable of a SingleSubstFormat1 lookup; the coverage iterator yields an uninitialized glyph id, which flows into hb_set_t::has -> page_for -> page_map.bsearch and is used as an uninitialized comparison operand inside hb_vector_t::bfind. Crash State: bfind<page_map_t> <- bsearch<page_map_t> <- hb_set_t::page_for.

source.value_from: the Coverage subtable of the GSUB SingleSubstFormat1 lookup in the attacker-controlled input font (this+coverage); a malformed/degenerate coverage table drives the iterator over which glyph ids are materialized
source.description: Project-level materialization point: the closure loop constructs a Coverage iterator directly over the parsed, untrusted GSUB coverage subtable. The glyph ids consumed by the loop originate here from attacker-controlled font structure, not from the fuzzer harness entry.

sink.description: MSan use-of-uninitialized-value: the binary-search comparison result c = arrayZ[mid].cmp(&x) is derived from the uninitialized key.major (get_major of the uninitialized glyph id), so branching on c > 0 reads an uninitialized value. This is the reported crash location.

root_cause.description: The Coverage iterator does not guarantee that get_glyph() returns an initialized glyph id for a malformed/degenerate coverage subtable. The iterator's glyph state (j for format-2 / glyphArray[i] for format-1) is derived from unvalidated range/glyph records, and SingleSubstFormat1::closure then consumes iter.get_glyph() unconditionally. There is no well-formedness validation of the coverage records that would make the produced glyph id defined, so an uninitialized glyph id escapes into the set-membership lookup. NOTE: the ARVO-recorded fixed_commit c0a3f38 is a 'Fix distcheck' Makefile.sources change and is NOT the semantic memory-safety fix; the actual hardening of the coverage-iterator initialization landed in a later upstream commit, so this root_cause is grounded in the sanitizer origin and vulnerable source rather than the recorded patch.

parser_admitted.note: The input font was accepted as a face, its GSUB table was located and dispatched, and the subset plan reached GSUB lookup closure. Entering SubstLookup closure over a real GSUB lookup confirms the font passed container/table dispatch and entered the vulnerable SingleSubst closure path.

tainted_value_origin.description: The uninitialized value becomes a first-class glyph id here: iter.get_glyph() returns the iterator's uninitialized glyph state. MSan reports the origin as the stack allocation of 'iter' in this function (hb-ot-layout-gsub-table.hh:41).

coarse_trace.summary: Fuzzer entry: wraps the input bytes as an hb_blob_t/hb_face_t and calls trySubset().
trySubset calls hb_subset() on the untrusted face.
hb_subset builds the subset plan via hb_subset_plan_create().
GID retention drives _gsub_closure() to expand glyphs reachable through GSUB.
Calls hb_ot_layout_lookups_substitute_closure() over the GSUB lookups.
Dispatches SubstLookup::closure for each GSUB lookup (parser-admitted checkpoint).
Dispatches to SingleSubst for lookup type Single.
Iterates the coverage subtable; reads an uninitialized glyph id and passes it to c->glyphs->has().
hb_set_t::has(glyph_id) forwards the uninitialized glyph to page_for().
page_for builds page_map_t key = {get_major(g)} from the uninitialized glyph and calls page_map.bsearch(key).
Binary search compares the uninitialized key.major; branching on the comparison result triggers the MSan use-of-uninitialized-value.

fine_trace.note: Untrusted-input load: constructs a Coverage iterator over the parsed, attacker-controlled coverage subtable (this+coverage) of the GSUB SingleSubstFormat1 lookup. hb_auto_t constructs iter and calls Coverage::Iter::init on the coverage table.

Root cause: the coverage iterator initialization derives its glyph state from unvalidated coverage records and does not guarantee that get_glyph() returns an initialized glyph for a malformed/degenerate coverage table. No well-formedness guard makes the produced glyph id defined before the closure loop consumes it. (Format-1 iteration reads c->glyphArray[i] symmetrically; the format-agnostic defect is the missing validation of the coverage records.) The recorded fixed_commit is a distcheck Makefile change, so this is grounded in source + the MSan origin (stack allocation of 'iter').
The uninitialized iterator glyph state becomes a first-class value: glyph_id = iter.get_glyph(). MSan attributes the origin to the stack allocation of 'iter' in this function (line 41).
The uninitialized glyph id is passed, unchecked, into the working glyph set membership test.
has(g) forwards the uninitialized glyph to page_for().
The uninitialized glyph is materialized into key.major via get_major(g). MSan reports the value is 'stored to memory' here (hb-set.hh:687:22) as part of the page_map_t key.
The uninitialized key is passed into the page_map binary search.
page_map_t::cmp computes (int) o->major - (int) major, i.e. it reads key.major (x = key), which is uninitialized. c inherits the uninitialized value.
Use-of-uninitialized-value: the binary-search control flow branches on the uninitialized comparison result c, which MSan flags as the crash. Reported at hb-vector.hh:214:16.

uninit_origin.description: Uninitialized value was created by the stack allocation of 'iter' in OT::SingleSubstFormat1::closure.

poc.trigger: Run the prebuilt hb-subset-fuzzer (libfuzzer_msan) on the PoC font ('arvo run' on n132/arvo:10097-vul). The malformed font contains a GSUB table with a SingleSubstFormat1 lookup whose Coverage subtable is degenerate, so the closure coverage iterator yields an uninitialized glyph id; MSan reports use-of-uninitialized-value in hb_vector_t::bfind.

format.name: OpenType/TrueType font (GSUB table)
format.contract: Candidate PoC must be admitted as an hb_face_t and reach GSUB lookup closure during hb_subset: it must present a parseable sfnt/font container with a GSUB table containing a SingleSubst (format 1) lookup whose Coverage subtable is malformed/degenerate enough that the coverage iterator produces an undefined glyph id. Parser-admission requires the GSUB table and lookup list to dispatch to SingleSubstFormat1::closure; the vulnerability-relevant state is the malformed coverage records of that lookup.
